positions.title: MLOps / Software Engineer
positions.description:
I build and lead technical infrastructure at Dayhoff Labs, a startup developing foundational AI models for biochemistry and synthetic biology. As the third hire, I've built most of the company's technical stack as we've grown to ~15 people.

**Infrastructure & DevOps**
- Overhauled our cloud infrastructure from manual GCP setups to automated, Terraform-managed AWS environments with least-privilege access and secure authentication
- Built containerized development environments that work seamlessly across GCP, AWS, and local Macs, with custom tooling I maintain and regularly update. This custom system avoided $50k+/year in third-party tooling costs
- Configured distributed computing systems on both GCP and AWS, dramatically scaling our capacity for large-scale bioinformatics processing

**Data & Research Systems** 
- Implemented a custom data management system based on DVC, giving our research team streamlined access to versioned datasets
- Established software engineering best practices for our academic research team, bridging research and industry standards

**Strategic Impact**
- Identified and eliminated technical bottlenecks that were slowing research progress
- Provided technical expertise for grant applications, combining bioengineering and software engineering perspectives
- Built the foundational technical infrastructure that enables our scientists to focus on AI-driven research rather than tooling

As an early team member, I take ownership of our entire technical stack and proactively solve infrastructure challenges before they impact research velocity.

positions.title: Senior Data Scientist
positions.description:
Very is a fully-distributed IoT engineering firm, partnering with clients to build systems for smart manufacturing, smart energy & utilities, consumer electronics, and connected wellness.

I worked with the full stack of software engineering needed to deploy data pipelines to production. My core competency is the Python data science stack (numpy, pandas, scikit-learn) and cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP, Terraform), but I’ve also built RESTful web applications in Django and used SQL to manage our databases. I live in the Linux CLI and Dockerized CI/CD pipelines, not in isolated Jupyter Notebooks. I practice Agile and test-driven development, setting the culture of small teams to understand clients' needs and deliver code.
positions.insights: Skills: Django · Machine Learning · Terraform · Python (Programming Language) · SQL · Data Science · Amazon Web Services (AWS)

positions.title: Assistant Data Science Instructor
positions.description:
As an independent contractor, I worked with Correlation One and the Colombian Ministry of Information and Communication Technology (MinTIC) to teach a 10-week training program in ML and Data Science, for 300 professionals chosen through a competitive application.

>> I managed hundreds of students through classes and projects.
>> I worked with the chief instructor (Natesh Pillai, professor of statistics at Harvard) to design and implement the final project in the curriculum.

positions.title: Senior Research Scientist
positions.description:
Hinge is an early-stage protein engineering startup.

>> Designed the company's first data processing pipeline in Python, replacing legacy methods handled in Excel.
>> Created in-depth literature reviews in cancer immunotherapy, resulting in three internal white papers used by the CEO during funding negotiations.
>> Wrote and managed four SBIR small-business grant applications, bringing in $125,000 of grant funding.

positions.title: Scientific Advisor
positions.description:
Open Philanthropy is a major private science funder.

>> Wrote scientific reports for non-technical decision makers, helping steer the organization's funding priorities in biotechnology and geoengineering.
>> Organized a major call for research proposals. Our team triaged 120+ proposals, recruited external reviewers, conducted due diligence, and finally directed more than $10 million in grant funding to four research projects in the life sciences.

positions.title: PhD, Bioengineering
positions.description:
Ed Boyden's group develops tools to map, control, and repair the brain. 

My PhD focused on molecular tools to manipulate genetic molecules and program them into artificial living systems. I designed and built a new class of programmable RNA-binding proteins and a new method for designing genetic circuits using Synthetic Minimal Cells.  My work led to two patents and two co-first-author publications, in PNAS and Nature Chemistry.

publications.title: Co-occurrence, possible origin, and health-risk assessment of arsenic and fluoride in drinking water sources in Mexico: Geographical data visualization
publications.publisher: Science of the Total Environment · Aug 29, 2019

publications.title: Expansion microscopy of zebrafish for neuroscience and developmental biology studies
publications.publisher: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences · Oct 25, 2017

patents.title: Engineering genetic circuit interactions within and between synthetic minimal cells and use thereof
Universal RNA-binding Protein Based on the Pumilio Domain Architecture
patents.description: We have conceived and developed a protein technology that enables binding to arbitrary sequences of RNA in living cells. Our technology is based on the Pumilio domain architecture, which we have developed into two variants called PumHD and Pumby.
